RT @LiveOverflow: I took a closer look at the https://t.co/rtT8YaMOFZ CTF, which aims to demonstrate that PHP2SHELL is not realistically exploitable. So I gave it a try.

Note: My analysis could be wrong, and I'm more than happy to be proven otherwise.

Here’s what I found:
• The server responds with Server: nginx and X-Powered-By: PHP/8.4.26.
• My differential fingerprinting scanner independently confirmed at least PHP 8.2+
• Hypotheses: I considered two possible setups:
    ◦ nginx → PHP-FPM
    ◦ nginx → Apache → PHP-FPM/mod_php
• After comparing the server's behavior against local test environments, the closest match appears to be nginx → PHP cli-server.

Plot twist: the response behavior is consistent with the PHP cli-server serving a static index.html rather than an index.php. If that's indeed the case, the challenge appears to be intentionally made unexploitable.

My conclusion (for now) is that I'm questioning whether this is a good-faith challenge.

Happy to be corrected if I've missed something!

As I argue in my upcoming report on "Global Electricity Undersupply" (learn about our reports here: https://t.co/kEx5Z4BJH7), China's electricity advantages remain an underestimated edge in the AI arms race, especially as models rapidly grow in size. Chinese models continue to widen the gap with US models in terms of token usage. Just between October 5th and 11th, AI models worldwide processed 172 trillion tokens, with Chinese models accounting for 86.74 trillion of those tokens versus 18.97 trillion for US AI models, according to OpenRouter data. It was the 24th consecutive week in which Chinese models outpaced US models in token usage. This has continued to put downward pressure on token prices, with the LLM Token Expenditure Index falling by more than half since this summer, begging even more questions about the unit economics of US hyperscalers versus their Chinese competitors. The US bet is that bigger and therefore, smarter models are their competitive advantage over China. It’s staggering how rapidly frontier models are growing. As The New York Times reported recently:

"In 2026, GPT 6 Astra took nearly an octillion calculations to train—over 50 million times as many calculations as GPT 1 did. Even calling this figure astronomical understates its size: An octillion is a thousand times the number of stars in the known universe…Researchers predict that by 2030, training the largest A.I. models may use electricity at a rate similar to New York City today."

The bigger models get, the more electricity they demand and therefore, the bigger China’s advantage becomes given their electricity supply capacity and pricing. According to Wall Street Journal reporting from late last year, Chinese data center power rates range between 3 and 5.6¢ per kWh while US data center power rates range between 7 and 9.1¢ per kWh.

Far more to come in the report!
